name: One or many
rule: A number word before a thing means more than one.
So the thing takes -s: three books, several friends.

wrong.text: She bought three new book for school.

right.text: She bought three new books for school.

spot: Look left of the thing for a count: two, many, several, a few, all.
deeper: 'One of the …' needs the plural too: one of the boys.
Some words do not end in -s: children, people, sheep.
'Each' and 'every' take one: every student, each book.
